title: Pandora's Tower
subtitle: A rescue measured in time away

body: Pandora's Tower is Ganbarion's Wii action role-playing game following Aeron's attempt to save Elena from a curse that is turning her into a monster. He explores thirteen towers in search of the flesh needed to reverse its effects, returning to an observatory where Elena waits. The journey connects combat and environmental puzzles with the condition of someone left behind. Every expedition therefore has a practical urgency: progress deeper into a tower must be weighed against the time that Elena can safely endure before Aeron comes back.

Aeron's Oraclos Chain binds enemies, pulls away armour and connects targets so that damage can be shared between them. Its usefulness extends into the towers' architecture, allowing him to grapple, climb and swing across gaps. A mechanism or platform can become another part of the same tool's vocabulary. The tower Masters remain locked behind environmental challenges, so reaching a boss involves understanding the route as well as surviving it. Combat and exploration continually ask the player to reconsider what can be caught, pulled or connected by the chain.

Bringing flesh to Elena reverses the curse for a time, but its usefulness deteriorates after it is collected. Talking with her, giving gifts and asking for help with tasks also affect the relationship recorded by the game. The observatory is therefore more than an equipment stop between battles. It is the place where the expedition's purpose becomes visible and where time spent together has consequences. Different endings respond to that bond, connecting the larger outcome with the pattern of departures, discoveries and returns made throughout the adventure.
